newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: BASS SAYS COMPLETES MERGER OF THREE CZECH BREWERS.
newsitem.headline: BASS SAYS COMPLETES MERGER OF THREE CZECH BREWERS.

text.p: Britain's Bass plc said on Tuesday it had completed a merger of its Prague Breweries a.s. unit, and two regional brewers creating the third largest Czech brewer with a 14 percent market share.

"Companies Ostravar a.s. and Pivovary Vratislavice nad Nisou were wound up without liquiditaion...the legal entity which has come into existence through the merger will be named after its largest unit - Prague Breweries," a statement from Bass said.
Bass, which took majority stakes in all three of its Czech holdings in 1996, holds a 55 percent share in the new brewery.
The statement said that the new company will have a registered capital of 1.7 billion crowns which will be divided into shares with a nominal value of 100 crowns each.

"With its annual output of 2.5 million hectolitres and its market share of 14 percent, new Prague Breweries will become one of the three largest brewing groupsa in the country. The merged company will employ 2,000 people," Bass said.
Bass made its first move in the Czech brewing industry at the beginning of 1994 when it took a 34 percent stake in Prague Brweries, whose flagship brand is Staropramen, for nine million pounds.
Late last year Bass took a 20 percent stake in one of the other major players in Czech brewing Pivovar Radgast a.s.

It subsequently raised its stake to 33 percent and said it was contemplating the possibility of a merger in the long term of Radegast and Prague Breweries to fulfil its aim of forming a brewing conglomerate with a 25-30 percent market share.

The Czech Republic boasts the world's highest per capita beer consumption and Bass says it is keen to take advantage of the country's centries old tradition of brewing in lucrative export markets in western Europe.
